_note: SYNTHETIC demo maintenance log written for the InfraGuard AI demo. Not real facility records.

records.text: CRAC Unit 1 supply air drifted from 24 C to 34 C over two hours. Air filter was clogged. Replaced filter, cleaned coil. Work took 2.5 h, parts and labor about $900. Temperature back to normal within 30 minutes.
CRAC Unit 1 fan speed dropped to 780 rpm and supply temperature rose above 32 C. Fan belt worn and slipping. Replaced belt and re-tensioned. Work took 3 h, about $1,400.

High temperature alarm on CRAC Unit 1. Refrigerant pressure low from a leak at a brazed joint. Leak repaired and unit recharged. Unit was down 6 h, repair about $3,800. Portable cooling was used for Hall A.
Quarterly preventive maintenance on CRAC Unit 1: filters replaced, belts inspected, condensate drain cleared. No faults found. 1.5 h.
Storage Node 7, Bay 3 drive reported 120 reallocated sectors and rising pending sectors. Data migrated, drive hot-swapped, RAID rebuild finished in 9 h. Swap took 45 minutes, drive cost about $320.
Storage Node 7 drive bays running at 41 C after a blocked rack vent. Vent cleared, drive temperatures returned to 32 C. No drive replaced. 1 h.

Fleet note: drives with uncorrectable errors (SMART 187/198) or growing pending sectors (SMART 197) are replaced proactively. Standard procedure: confirm backup, mark drive failed in controller, hot-swap, verify RAID rebuild. Typical swap 1 h, about $300 to $450 per drive.
Milling machine stopped on overstrain: torque above 60 Nm with tool wear near 200 min. Tool replaced and feed rate reduced. Machine down 5 h, repair about $2,600.
Power failure fault on milling machine at high rotational speed with high torque. Spindle drive inspected, settings corrected. 4 h, about $1,900.
Data hall policy: any CRAC unit above 32 C supply for more than 10 minutes requires a technician on site within 1 hour and a check of filters, fan belt and refrigerant pressure.
ASIC miner reported one fan at 0 rpm and chip temperature 92 C; the unit throttled to about 150 TH/s. Replaced the fan, about $35 and 20 min. Hashrate back to rated within 10 minutes.

ASIC miner hashrate dropped to about two thirds of rated with hardware error rate near 2%; one of three hashboards not detected. Swapped the hashboard from spare stock, about $480 and 45 min. Faulty board sent for repair.
Dust buildup on miner intake; chip temperature creeping up to 84 C and fan speed at maximum. Cleaned with compressed air, 10 min, no parts. Preventive cleaning avoided a hashboard failure.
Container fan wall M2 lost two of eight fans; intake air rose to 35 C and the miners in row M2 throttled. Replaced the fan motors, about $850 parts and labor, 3 h.
